**RA Progress Statement — Seoul–Daegu Honorific Shift Corpus**  
**Reporting date: November 9, 2026**  
**Prepared for the Winter 2027 funding review**

This statement provides context for the description of my annotation progress as “six weeks behind” at the November 6 lab meeting.

I am the only RA responsible for Korean annotation on this NSF-funded project. The fall-term target was 6,000 annotated utterances; as of this report, I have annotated 4,200. The relevant timeline is as follows:

- **September 3:** I sent Prof. Hollander the IRB amendment to add 14 new Daegu recordings for her signature. I was not permitted to work with those recordings until the amendment was signed.
- **September 12, September 24, and October 6:** I sent email reminders about the pending signature. I have retained these emails and the related correspondence.
- **October 15:** Prof. Hollander signed the amendment, ending the six-week period during which the new recordings were unavailable to me.
- **October 15–November 9:** I annotated approximately 1,900 utterances, averaging more than 500 per week. This exceeds the planned rate of 350 utterances per week.

During the waiting period, I also recoded all 2,300 existing utterances using the revised speech-level scheme Prof. Hollander requested in August. This recoding was not part of the original project timeline. It was substantive project work completed while annotation of the new recordings was blocked, and I ask that it be counted as progress rather than treating that period as inactivity.

There are 1,800 utterances remaining to reach the fall target. Based on my current annotation rate, I expect to reach 6,000 annotated utterances by the end of January 2027.

For the funding review, I ask that any reference to my being “six weeks behind” include the reason for that gap: the IRB amendment awaited signature from September 3 until October 15, and I could not annotate the new recordings during that period. Alternatively, I ask that the “behind” comment be omitted from the review record. Without this context, the comment does not accurately represent either the cause of the delay or my productivity once access to the recordings was restored.
